meta_title: MyPack: turn any website into a desktop app
meta_description: MyPack turns a website or a local HTML project into a standalone desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux in a few clicks. No toolchain. Free and open source: no app limits, no license keys, no account.
meta_og_image_alt: The MyPack icon on a cobalt background, with the words: Any website. Any desktop.
hero_lede: Turn a website, or a local HTML project, into a real, standalone desktop app in a few clicks. No Go, Rust, Node or Xcode project required.
hero_note: Free and open source under Apache-2.0. Every feature included: no app limits, no license keys, no account.
demo_aria: A website window turns into its app icon, gets a verified badge, and drops into the Dock.
steps_lede: Paste a URL, confirm the name and icon, build, then install and open. Most builds take seconds.
step1_d: Click New App (⌘N) and paste an address, for example github.com. You can also drop an HTML file or a folder onto the window, or pick a site from the suggestions.
step1_alt: New App: an address field with a list of popular websites
step2_d: MyPack fetches the name and the best icon. Change either, then choose how the app looks: window, compact, sidebar or menu bar, its title bar and its size.
step2_alt: New App with Figma's name and icon, a window preview and the Look & Behaviour settings
step3_d: MyPack doesn't compile anything. It writes your app's settings into a small prebuilt runtime, and shows each step as it goes.
step3_alt: A build in progress: step 3 of 5, Make it an app
step4_t: Use it like any other app
step4_d: The app is installed and opened in one click, with its own name, icon, window and sign-in. It keeps working even if you uninstall MyPack.
step4_alt: The finished app: installed and opened, with its size and build time
why_title: A browser tab is a poor home for an app
why_lede: Tabs get lost among other tabs, every site shares one set of cookies, and none of them get their own Dock icon, notifications or window. MyPack gives each site a proper app of its own, and then keeps looking after it.
why1_d: MyPack uses a small prebuilt runtime and writes your app's settings into it, so a build takes seconds. The runtime downloads once, signed and verified.
why2_t: Apps that stand on their own
why2_d: Every app has its own name, icon and separate sign-in, uses the system WebView, and keeps working if you uninstall MyPack.
why3_d: Update an app in one click without losing your logins. If an update fails, the previous version comes back. Repair it, or move it to another computer.
gallery_lede: Real screens from the current app, in demo mode.
g_library_d: The Library: your apps, groups and drafts, with updates and anything that needs attention at the top.
g_discover_d: Discover: dozens of popular sites, one click to start. Anyone can add more on GitHub.
g_builds_d: Builds: every build with its status, platform and duration, from the app, the CLI or an agent.
g_palette_d: ⌘K finds any app, page or action without leaving the keyboard.
g_menubar_d: The menu bar: paste an address, jump to a recent app and follow builds without opening the window.
feat_lede: No app limits, no license keys, no account. Every feature below is in the free download.
f_make1_d: MyPack fetches the name and the best icon. Change both, or design an icon in the Icon Studio.
f_make2_d: An HTML file, a folder with index.html, or a Vite, CRA, Astro, Nuxt, SvelteKit or Next export. The project's build runs only after you approve it.
f_make3_d: Dozens of popular sites, one click to start. The list is a plain JSON file anyone can add to.
f_make4_d: Several sites in one window, with a side rail, a separate session per site and split view.
f_make5_d: Bring your pake.json from Pake along.
f_in1_d: Web notifications, and a Dock badge for unread counts.
f_in2_d: Media keys and Now Playing for music and video sites.
f_in3_d: Links between your MyPack apps open in the right app.
f_in4_d: Normal, compact, sidebar, or in the menu bar.
f_in6_d: Content blocking, custom CSS and JavaScript, proxy and user-agent settings.
f_in7_d: Sign-in pop-ups from Google, Microsoft and others just work.
f_man1_d: Everything you made, with Install & Open, Update, Repair and Uninstall.
f_man2_d: Sync the Library across computers through a shared folder such as iCloud Drive, or export and import .mypack files.
f_man3_d: An optional extension turns the tab you're on into an app.
f_man4_d: English, 繁體中文, 简体中文, 粵語, Español, Français and 日本語.
cmp_lede: Plenty of good tools turn websites into apps. Here's where MyPack differs, as plainly as we can put it.
cmp_r_app: A desktop app to make and manage your apps
cmp_tool_rust: Needs Rust and Node.js for local builds
cmp_thanks: MyPack owes a lot to Pake, which showed how good a website can feel as a small, focused desktop app. MyPack reads Pake configs, so you can bring yours along.
cmp_note: Based on each project's public pages in November 2026. Something out of date?
install_lede: Download the installer, or use the package manager you already have. Each one puts a mypack command on your PATH and keeps MyPack updated.
support_mac: The main platform. Apple silicon and Intel. Apps use WKWebView.
support_linux: x64 and arm64. Apps use WebKitGTK, tested on Ubuntu 24.04.
support_win: x64 and arm64. Apps use WebView2, less tested so far.
install_mac: A .dmg for Apple silicon and Intel, or Homebrew:
install_win: Setup programs for x64 and arm64, or winget, Scoop or Chocolatey:
install_linux: .deb and .rpm packages for x64 and arm64, or your package manager:
install_unsigned: Releases aren't signed yet. On macOS, if Gatekeeper blocks the first launch, right-click MyPack.app and choose Open. On Windows, SmartScreen may ask you to confirm: More info, then Run anyway.
install_all: Plain archives of the app and the CLI are on every release too.
dev_p1: The app's binary is also the CLI. With --json, every command prints one JSON object, and exit codes are stable.
dev_p2: A built-in MCP server lets Claude Code, Codex and other agents list, create and build apps for you. They can't install apps, and a project's build script only runs after you approve it.
dev_p3: MyPack itself has no built-in chat or LLM.
dev_c_create: a draft project, then build, install and open it
